note: Boulders (Dave 2026-10-21): not rocks; a pick (or a stone axe, 3 times slower) breaks them into rough stones. The yield is plain math from the size: volume (an ellipsoid of the boulder's radius and height_ratio x radius high, the buried part included) x density x yield, divided by the mass of one stone (weights.json, 1 kg), is the number of stones; a 1 m radius boulder makes about 4600, 0.3 m about 125, 1.2 m about 7900 at yield 0.5. One blow with an iron or steel pick takes one stone; whacks_per_stone is by the tool's material (items.json material) and applies to the best tool on the hotbar; a stone axe takes 3 blows per stone. The boulder shrinks as stones come out (cube root of what is left) and is gone with the last one; what is left is saved (world_items.json boulders). Every blow wears the tool like other work (durability in items.json, drops.json tool_wear per_use may add more). Boulders are server-owned and laid out like loose stones: per 32 m cell, up to max_per_cell, only where the ground rises more than min_slope or at a water bank, deterministic from the cell. size: radius_min..radius_max, radius_power > 1 makes small ones commoner. luck_extra: the chance that a blow's stone comes away as two (and takes two from the boulder), passed through the luck function (0 switches it off; 0.05 means about 5 percent at luck 0, about 7 percent at +10, 3.5 percent at -10).

ore.note: Ore and coal from boulders (guide finding F-23, FLINT_ORE_SPEC.md): a boulder that lies within reach_m of an ore body of the terrain (the geology's ore_bodies) is an outcrop with that ore with chance boulder_share (decided from the boulder's key, so it is the same every time). A PICK (not an axe) takes the ore: each piece that comes away is the ore with chance piece_share, else stone. Iron needs no better pick than copper: there is no bronze pick in the game, and an iron pick needs iron ore first (a circle), so the ladder is made by rarity, not by tool. items: ore name in data/tables/resources.json -> item id.

flint.note: Flint (guide finding F-02, FLINT_ORE_SPEC.md): each stone that comes off a boulder is a flint nodule instead with this chance, more near water. Bank stones (drops.json ground_scatter.bank.flint) are flint with their own chance. Flint makes the hide scraper, javelin and sickle.
